City Council Meeting Policy:
cityofpasadena.net/CityCouncilMeetingPolicy
Para facilitar la
participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente por medios
electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la siguiente manera:
1.
Ya sea que participen en persona o
virtualmente en la reunión, los miembros del público pueden proporcionar
comentarios públicos enviando una tarjeta de orador antes del comienzo de los
comentarios públicos sobre ese tema, en la siguiente página web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más
de un artículo del orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario
en línea (los oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso
publicado en la agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el
Consejo Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y
el Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2.
Participación
en reuniones en persona :
Complete una tarjeta de orador en línea en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Después de enviar una tarjeta de orador público, los miembros del público pueden
a sistir a la reunión en persona al acudir a la Cámara del
Concejo Municipal de
Pasadena, Sala
S249 en el Ayuntamiento en la fecha y hora de inicio de la reunión publicada.
Participación en la reunión virtua l: para los participantes virtuales,
puede asistir conectándose a la reunión mediante una computadora, otro
dispositivo electrónico
o por teléfono.
Revise la agenda para identificar la hora de inicio publicada para la
r eunión
y conéctese a la reunión justo antes o al comienzo de la reunión.
Para
participar en los comentarios públicos sobre un tema y ser reconocido para
hablar, se requiere que el orador inicie sesión en la reunión con el mismo
nombre o
número de
teléfono que se usó en el formulario de la Tarjeta de orador. Esto permitirá que
el personal de la Ciudad ubique y ascienda al orador a la reunión
cuando sea el
momento de su comentario público. Las llamadas telefónicas de los participantes
a la reunión del Concejo Municipal se grabarán como parte de la
reunión del Concejo
Municipal. Al permanecer en línea y hacer comentarios públicos
durante la reunión del Concejo Municipal por teléfono, usted acepta que se
grabe su llamada
telefónica. A continuación se muestra la información de conectividad para la
participación virtual:
Computadora o
dispositivos electrónicos, únase a la reunión en:
cityofpasadena.net/cczoom
Marcación
telefónica únicamente: 1-669-900-6833, ID de reunión: 161 482 446
3. Línea de ayuda con
la tarjeta de orador : si un orador de comentario público necesita ayuda
para completar una tarjeta de orador, llame a la oficina del secretario
municipal al: (626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda se abrirá 30 minutos antes de la
hora de inicio publicada de la reunión.
4. Los miembros del
público pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier extensión antes del inicio de
la reunión, a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La correspondencia se enviará al Concejo Municipal
antes del inicio de la reunión, se publicará en línea y formará parte del
registro legislativo del tema.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  April 19, 2023 - 5:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 6:39 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Williams.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Felicia Williams
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas (Arrived at 6:41 p.m.)

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

REMOTE PARTICIPATION  APPROVAL OF A REQUEST BY COUNCILMEMBER RIVAS TO
REQUEST  PARTICIPATE  REMOTELY  DUE  TO  EMERGENCY
  CIRCUMSTANCES

  Mayor Gordo stated the following: "I received an email on
  Wednesday, April 12, 2023 from Councilmember Jess Rivas
  requesting that the City Council allow her to participate remotely for
  the special City Council meeting on Wednesday, April 19, 2023, due
  to emergency circumstance pursuant to Government Code Section
  54953 [(F)(2)(A)(ii)], and that she is following her physicians order
  placing her off work for a medical condition that prevents her from
  attending in person."

  It was moved by Councilmember Lyon, seconded by
  Councilmember Madison, to approve the request by
  Councilmember Rivas to participate remotely in today's City Council
  meeting due to emergency circumstances as described in her
  communication to the City Council dated April 12, 2023, subject to
  the requirements of Government Code Section 54953. (Motion
  unanimously approved) (Absent: Councilmember Rivas)

Councilmember Rivas joined  Mayor Gordo read the following statement: "While I believe I am
the meeting at 6:41 p.m.  able to participate in this evening's meeting, consistent with my prior
  recusals on this matter and in order to ensure that the integrity of
  this important process, which we all want to be successful, is
  beyond reproach, out of abundance of caution, I will recuse myself
  from the appointment process of the [Pasadena] Rental Housing

Council Minutes  04/19/2023
   Board, because I own rental property in the City of Pasadena. Now
  let me be clear, I am seeking further advice from the FPPC in order
  to ask for clarity on future participation in the appointment process
  of the Rental Housing Board. But at this point in time, out of an
  abundance of caution, and to ensure that this process is beyond
  reproach and has the best chance to succeed, I will recuse myself
  and hand the gavel to Vice Mayor Williams."

Mayor Gordo recused  APPOINTMENT OF SEVEN TENANT MEMBERS, ONE
himself and left the meeting  AL TERNA TE TENANT MEMBER, FOUR AT-LARGE MEMBERS,
at 6:44 p.m.  AND ONE AL TERNA TE AT-LARGE MEMBER TO THE
  PASADENA RENTAL HOUSING BOARD (PRHB) (City Clerk)
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1)  Find that the proposed actions are exempt from review
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") in
  accordance with State CEQA Guidelines § 15061 (b)(3), the
  "common sense" provision that CEQA only applies to projects that
  may have a significant effect on the environment; and
  (2)  Approve the nominations and make initial appointments to
  the Pasadena Rental Housing Board in accordance with City
  Charter Sections 1811 (c) and (d), as follows:
  •  Seven Tenant Members (one from each Council District)
  o Four Members to serve four-year terms
  o Three Members to serve two-year terms
  •  One Alternate Tenant Member (citywide) to serve a
  four-year term
  •  Four At-Large Members (citywide)
  o Two Members to serve four-year terms
  o Two Members to serve two-year terms
  •  One Alternate At-Large Member (citywide) to serve a
  four-year term

  Vice Mayor Williams provided an overview of the meeting format
  and announced that public comment will be heard after the City
  Clerk's presentation.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, presented a PowerPoint presentation on
  the item, and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns regarding appointing
  applicants to the PRHB that are active parties in a lawsuit that
  challenges the validity of Measure H, and asked that the City
  Attorney identify any applicants that are parties in that litigation.

  Councilmember Hampton expressed appreciation to the City Clerk
  and staff for organizing the information; thanked the public and all
  the applicants who applied; and expressed the importance to him
  that the individuals appointed will view the issues collectively, as a
  whole, and not just view the issue from one side.

Council Minutes  2  04/19/2023
   In response to Councilmember Madison, City Attorney Bagneris
  provided the following Plaintiff names: Ahni Dodge, Simon Gibbons,
  Margaret Morgan, Danielle Moskowitz, and Tyler Werrin. She also
  named the lnterveners: Michelle White, Ryan Bell, and Affordable
  Pasadena. She noted that the City Charter Article XVIII establishes
  the qualifications for appointment to the PRHB, stating there is no
  language in the Charter that states someone who is party to
  litigation, or who challenges the measure, is ineligible to serve.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that the City Clerk's Office
  received twenty-seven letters expressing opposition to the City
  Council appointing all or some of the following applicants to the
  Pasadena Rental Housing Board; Penny Carter (1 letter), Ahni
  Dodge (15 letters), Simon Gibbons (23 letters), Tyler Werrin (21
  letters), Daniel Gonzalez (3 letters), Terry Tomek (17 letters),
  Barbara Pitts (1 letter), Emanuel Najera (1 letter), Allison Henry (1
  letter); and forty-seven letters in support of the City Council
  appointing all or some of the following applicants to the PRHB:
  Brandon Lamar (11 letters), Paulette Brown (2 letters), Peter Dreier
  (7 letters), Thea Orozco (5 letters), Arnold Siegel (5 letters), Ira
  West (7 letters), Aaron Markowitz (7 letters), James Edward Greely
  (2 letters), Adela Torres (2 letters), Simon Ybarra (1 letter), Ryan

  Robert Escobedo (5 letters), Gian McCoy (3 letters), Yaneli Soriano

  letter), Ahni Dodge (2 letters), Simon Gibbons (2 letters), Tyler
  Werrin (2 letters), Diane Romero Chavez (1 letter), Deborah Dunlop
  (1 letter). In addition, one letter advocating for the City Council to
  appoint members to the PRHB that will act in good faith; one letter
  advocating for the City Council to not appoint any landlords to the
  PRHB; and three letters advocating for the City Council to consider
  appointing landlords to the PRHB in an equal manner to tenant
  applicants, and/or expressing concerns with short notice of the
  special meeting to the community; were received by the City Clerk's
